title: Calcification in TAVI Prostheses: Correlation of Calcification Hotspots with Mechanical Stress and Thrombotic Deposits
summary: Artificial Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) heart valves can show initial signs of wear, such as calcium deposits, after 10-15 years. At that point, a new artificial heart valve may be necessary. Our population is aging, and more and more young people are receiving TAVI valves. Therefore, it is crucial that artificial heart valves have a particularly long lifespan. Much research is being conducted to improve artificial valves, but we still don't know enough about the causes of damage. In particular, the processes that lead to calcification of artificial heart valves are not yet fully understood. We have produced an artificial TAVI heart valve in the laboratory and can use it to investigate what causes calcification. To determine whether the same processes occur in patients, we would like to compare images of TAVI heart valves from patients with images of the TAVI heart valve from the laboratory. In this way, we aim to improve TAVI heart valves and make them more durable in the future.
conditions: Mechanical complication of heart valve prosthesis

interventions.name: Prospective and retrospective collection of computed tomography (CT) data and patient data of degenerated/calcified Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) prostheses as part of follow-up examinations after TAVI implantation or in preparation for repeat aortic valve replacement.
Analysis of calcification patterns in patient CT data and comparison with computed tomography data from experimentally in vitro degenerated/calcified prosthesis prototypes.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All patients presenting for TAVI follow-up with suspected dysfunction, degeneration, or failure of the bioprosthesis will be included. Furthermore, all patients presenting for examination in preparation for repeat valve replacement due to dysfunction or degeneration of the existing TAVI prosthesis will be included.
These inclusion criteria also apply to the retrospective part of the study.
Exclusion criteria:
he following are excluded from the prospective part of the study:
- underage patients
- Patients with psychiatric disorders and resulting legal incapacity
